chunks: From him, from Abdullah ibn Muskān, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, who said:

I asked Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) about the one who is rejected among the witnesses. He said, 'The ḍannīn and the opposing party.' I said, 'Then what about the fāsiq and the khā'in?' He said, 'All of these fall under the category of the ḍannīn.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the rejected witnesses according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refines the legal standards for witness admissibility by categorizing the 'ḍannīn' (those prone to conjecture) and the 'khāṣim' (the opposing party in a dispute) as primary grounds for rejection. He further clarifies that common defects such as being a 'fāsiq' (dissolute) or 'khā'in' (treacherous) are subsumed under the broader epistemological category of the 'ḍannīn', highlighting a nuanced Shia jurisprudential approach that links moral integrity with cognitive reliability in legal testimony.
